title: Mandela Invites His Prosecutor to Lunch
text:
In 1963 and 1964 Percy Yutar was the state prosecutor at the Rivonia Trial, where Nelson Mandela and his comrades were tried for sabotage and conspiracy against the apartheid state. Yutar prosecuted the case aggressively. The accused faced a possible death sentence, and Mandela and most of the others were sentenced to life imprisonment. Mandela remained in prison until 1990, twenty seven years after his arrest in 1962.

In 1994 Mandela became President of South Africa. In November 1995 he invited Yutar, by then an old man, to lunch at his official residence in Pretoria. The meal was kosher, out of respect for Yutar's Jewish faith. Afterward Yutar spoke to reporters about the President's kindness and said he had only been doing his duty under the law of the time.

The lunch was one of several deliberate gestures Mandela made that year toward former adversaries, including a visit to Betsie Verwoerd, widow of the architect of apartheid. Many people, including some of his own supporters, found them hard to accept. Mandela saw them as a way to show white South Africans that the new government would not seek revenge.
lesson: Reconciliation becomes believable when you reach out personally to the people who wronged you. Such gestures cost pride, but they can reassure a whole frightened community.
source: Contemporary South African press reports (November 1995); Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorized Biography (1999)
